name: dmagnetic
why: An interpreter for Magnetic Scrolls text adventures, a strange old-school environment that few have ever run.

brief.what_it_is: dMagnetic is a terminal-based interpreter for Magnetic Scrolls text adventures, the 1980s-90s Magnetic Scrolls games. It runs classic interactive fiction titles, named on the page as The Pawn, The Guild of Thieves, Jinxter, Myth, Fish!, Corruption and Wonderland, on modern computers. It takes the original game files as input, which the homepage lists as .mag/.gfx, MS-DOS binaries, Magnetic Windows .RSC files, and disk images for Commodore 64 (.d64), Amstrad CPC (.DSK), Archimedes (.adf/.adl), Spectrum +3 (.dsk), Atari XL (.atr) and Apple II (.nib/.2mg). Output is the game played in a terminal window, with optional graphics rendered as text, ANSI, UTF-8 blocks or sixels.
brief.why_it_exists: The page says dMagnetic is an interpreter that lets people play the classic Magnetic Scrolls adventures on modern computers, and that it was designed for portability so it can be compiled on anything with a C compiler. The author also says the games are not included: dMagnetic is not a game itself and requires the original binaries to run.
brief.how_it_works: The interpreter reads the original Magnetic Scrolls game data from the supported file formats and runs it inside a TTY or terminal. Because the games are played in a terminal, the classic pictures are rendered in one of several modes: None, Monochrome ASCII art, Low ANSI, High ANSI with more colours, UTF (UTF-8 characters used as pixels), or Sixel where the terminal supports it (the page mentions mlterm and xterm -ti vt340). The author also has a separate write-up on the data structures, linked as dMagnetic_datastructures.pdf.

brief.install_notes: Packages exist for OpenBSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew and Termux (pkg install dMagnetic). Building from source needs only a C compiler, following the wget, tar, make, sudo make install sequence on the homepage. The interpreter does not come with games: you must supply the original Magnetic Scrolls binaries or disk images yourself, for example from the Magnetic Scrolls memorial site the page mentions. The page gives no first-run steps beyond that.
brief.standout: The interpreter reproduces the look of Magnetic Scrolls' graphics inside an ordinary terminal, using ASCII, ANSI, UTF-8 block pixels or sixel, and it reads original disk images from many 8-bit and 16-bit platforms, not only the PC binaries. It is a rare modern way to run these games at all.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. The current release is dMagnetic 0.37, dated 16 May 2023, and the page offers previous releases. I did not check a repository commit history or a changelog, so the most recent activity I can confirm is that 2023 release.
brief.caveats: It is not a game and does not include any game files; you need the original binaries or disk images. It runs only in a terminal, so the full graphics need a terminal that supports sixel or similar. The homepage is a personal site with many unrelated projects, and the README-style text was thin on build details beyond the listed commands. I did not open the linked documentation PDF or the screenshots and videos. Licence is BSD 2-clause, as the page states.
quotes: dMagnetic is not a game itself. It requires the original binaries to run.
It has been designed with portability in mind, and can be compiled on anything with a C-Compiler.
It has been published under the BSD 2-clause license, so it does not have to stop there.

judge.reason: A portable interpreter for obscure classic adventures that reconstructs their graphics in the terminal and reads game data from a striking range of vintage disk formats.

entry.title: dMagnetic
entry.tldr: A terminal interpreter that runs 1980s Magnetic Scrolls text adventures like The Pawn and Jinxter from their original game files, with pictures drawn as text or sixels.
entry.deeper_look:
dMagnetic plays the text adventures published by Magnetic Scrolls in the 1980s and 90s: The Pawn, The Guild of Thieves, Jinxter, Myth, Fish!, Corruption and Wonderland. It is an interpreter, not a game. It reads the original game data and runs it in your terminal.

It accepts an unusual range of inputs. The homepage lists .mag/.gfx files, MS-DOS binaries, Magnetic Windows .RSC files, and disk images from the Commodore 64, Amstrad CPC, Archimedes, Spectrum +3, Atari XL and Apple II. The same adventures shipped on many incompatible machines, and one program can open the data from all of them.

These games had illustrations, which is the odd part in a terminal. dMagnetic can draw them in several modes: none, monochrome ASCII art, low or high ANSI colour, UTF-8 characters used as pixels, or sixel graphics where the terminal supports it. The page mentions mlterm and `xterm -ti vt340` for sixel.

The idea underneath is preservation through portability. The author says it was "designed with portability in mind, and can be compiled on anything with a C-Compiler." The game files are a small virtual machine's program, so a small interpreter keeps them playable on machines that did not exist when they were written. The author also has a separate write-up of the data structures, linked from the homepage as a PDF.
entry.install:
brew install dMagnetic
# The game files are not included. You must supply original Magnetic Scrolls binaries or disk images yourself; the homepage points to a Magnetic Scrolls memorial site.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the options, including how to point it at a game file and choose a graphics mode.

entry.whats_unique: It reads original disk images from many 8-bit and 16-bit platforms, not just PC binaries, and renders the old pictures in a plain terminal as ASCII, ANSI, UTF-8 blocks or sixel.
entry.caveats: It ships with no games, so you need to find the original Magnetic Scrolls files yourself, and full graphics need a sixel-capable terminal.
